title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving nutrition assistance to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas of Qansax Dheere

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will deliver a 12-month integrated nutrition response aimed at improving the nutritional status of vulnerable populations in Qansax Dheere District—an area prioritized under Somalia’s 2025 HNRP. Qansax Dheere continues to face persistently high levels of acute malnutrition, compounded by limited nutrition services and recurring climatic and socio-economic shocks that weaken household food security and resilience.ltbrgtThe project will provide life-saving preventive and curative nutrition services for children under five and PLW. Services will be delivered through one Stabilization Centre (SC) at Ahmed Gurey Health Centre, two fixed Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) sites at Ahmed Gurey and Busley, and two mobile OTP teams serving Wadajir MCH, Korinbod, and October OTP. Nutrition commodities, including Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), therapeutic milks F-75 and F-100, and essential medicines will be obtained from UNICEF to ensure a consistent supply chain.ltbrgtEarly identification and referral of malnutrition cases will be strengthened through trained Community Health Workers (CHWs) and the Family MUAC approach, which empowers caregivers to detect malnutrition at home. Quarterly mass MUAC and edema screenings will be conducted using the Nutrition Cluster’s Kobo Toolbox platform. These efforts will be aimed at achieving zero Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases across the targeted communities through strengthened early detection and timely referral systems.ltbrgtSAM with and without medical complications will be treated at URRO-run Stabilization Centre and OTP sites. Children with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) will be treated at URRO OTP sites using the Expanded Admission Criteria (EAC), while MAM-affected PLW will be referred to partner-managed sites for treatment.ltbrgtTo address the root causes of malnutrition, the project will integrate Maternal, Infant, Young Child, and Adolescent Nutrition (MIYCAN) through Care Groups and structured behavior change communication. Key messages will promote breastfeeding, hygiene, WASH, and household food security. Prevention will take a Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) approach centered around the promotion of Tom Brown porridge and the One Egg Per Day campaign to improve the nutritional status of children and PLW. This will be complemented by micronutrient supplementation to prevent and treat micronutrient deficiencies.ltbrgtThe project will prioritize inclusion of marginalized and minority populations through targeted mapping and needs assessment. Efforts will be made to ensure meaningful participation through accessible feedback channels, inclusive language, and the recruitment of minority staff. Disaggregated data will be used to monitor and evaluate the reach and effectiveness of inclusive strategies.ltbrgtProtection will be integrated heavily throughout the project, with a strong focus on voucher-based support being delivered transparently to the most in need. Information will be widely disseminated on the available complaints and feedback mechanisms. Community-based structures and committees will be engaged as part of local coping capacity to respond to protection risks, particularly risks of exclusion and marginalization. Roles and responsibilities of gatekeepers—especially around PSEA—will be clearly defined and formalized through community agreements that limit their influence over aid access and reduce the risk of abuse or favoritism.ltbrgtAdditional protection mainstreaming components include GBV risk mitigation, child protection, inclusion of PWDs and minorities, and prevention of post-distribution aid diversion (PDAD). GBV and protection risk assessments will be conducted for caregivers of admitted children, with psychosocial support and referrals to legal aid, case management, and healthcare services facilitated. Confidential and accessible complaint and feedback mechanisms will support community accountability and ongoing program adaptation.ltbrgtlt/pgt
